The desired behaviour of the function `simlib_coadd.exe` is to combine observations within 0.4 days into a single co-added observation for each passband. At the moment, this only works if the observations in the same passband are consecutive. 

It would be great if the function `simlib_coadd.exe` also worked for non-consecutive observations, or at least to have a setting to choose what we wanted to do (I can imagine wanting non-consecutive observations to be separate for analysing fast transients).

comments.body:
Here is a small un-coadded SIMLIB so that the coadd program can be quickly tested: [uncoadd_not_ordered.simlib.txt](https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/files/8177165/uncoadd_not_ordered.simlib.txt) 
Note that the extension is `.simlib.txt` because GitHub does not accept `.simlib`, so do change the name of the extension when using it.

If we select the option to coadd all the observations in the same night of the same filter, the result should be:
* day 60235 -> Y, i, r (the order does not matter)
* day 60250 -> Y, i (the order does not matter)

Here is the full DDF simlib file zipped: [baseline_v2.0_10yrs_DDF_before_COADD.simlib.zip](https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/files/8193444/baseline_v2.0_10yrs_DDF_before_COADD.simlib.zip). You can also find this file on Cori at `/global/cfs/cdirs/lsst/groups/SN/snana/SURVEYS/LSST/USERS/SIMLIB_DEV/baseline_v2.0_10yrs_DDF_before_COADD.simlib`

Try new option
   simlib_coadd.exe <simlib> SORT_BAND

on Midway or Cori. The LSST-DDF test shows very small differences for <10% of rows; 1E-4 change in MJD or PSF. These small changes are likely due to replacing old float variables with double as part of refactor.
I used this setting to generate a new coadded simlib, make light curves and verified that it also works for non-consecutive observations. I am happy this issue is solved.

body:
A long time ago the sim-input reader was updated to abort on duplicate keys in the input file while allowing command-line overrides. However, the implementation works only for keys in the same file ... a duplicate key in the primary input and INCLUDE file does not trigger abort. Allowing duplicate keys in separate files is risky because there is no obvious hierarchy and can lead to mistakes if a change is made in only one of the files. 

Plan is to implement this abort-check as originally intended: abort on duplicates regardless of input file or include file. However, an INCLUDE file passed via command line is treated like any other command-line override and will not cause abort. This update may cause some aborts and perhaps find a few input key mistakes.

comments.body: Implemented in v11_04f

body: Redshift bin at zmax was mistakenly excluded from SIMSED flux-integral grid, and thus the last redshift bin was at zmax-zbin. For z > zmax-zbin, the SED flux-integral was used at zmax-zbin rather than interpolated. The correct distance was used, so the error here is in the K-correction. As an extreme example, SLSN in PLASTICC were generated out to 3.45, but the last z-bin was stored at z=2.7. Thus events for z>2.7 were K-corrected based on z=2.7 rather than interpolated between 2.7 and 3.45. This bug affects the highest redshift bin where events are noisy, and thus it would be difficult to notice this bug in an analysis.

comments.body: Fixed bug. SIMSED binaries should be re-generated.
Propagated fix to Cori and re-made SIMSED binaries for LSST.

comments.body: HOSTGAL_sSFR is an allowed data variable (along with HOSTLIB_LOGMASS), but it isn't yet determined by the simulation. I vaguely recall adding the HOSTGAL_sSFR variable as a placeholder in case we decided that we needed it. Your HOSTLIB uses LOG_SFR and it seems to be getting passed correctly to the output. If you want, we can teach the sim to recognize sSFR or SFR in the HOSTLIB and fill output HOSTGAL_sSFR with something meaningful.
Could you point me to an output fits file where SIM_HOSTLIB(LOGMASS_TRUE) and SIM_HOSTLIB(LOG_SFR) are correctly written?

I finally see the buggy output in the FITS output. This bug was caused by a recent zbug session where we defined SIM_HOSTLIB for two galaxies, but didn't update the FITS storage variable to hold 2 values ... so the 2nd value of -9 was overwriting the first value. Bug fix is pushed to GitHub and cori.

For this case, T_expose grid is very course (100, 1,000, 10,000, 100,000 sec) and linear interpolation of effective ZP vs. T_expose works poorly. Refactored to interpolate ZP vs. log10(T_expose) [instead of vs. T_expose], and SNR vs. T_expose is more sensible.

body: Some models (e.g. KN) will be found preferentially at high angular separation. When generating transient simulations for these models, SNANA currently creates an angular offset from the host position using the light profile, which will result in most generated objects being near the center of the host. While it is possible to scale the light profile, there's no way to avoid an overdensity at lower distances. While there is a MAXDDLR keyword to control how far away the simulation can be for an association, there is no corresponding MINDDLR keyword to exclude some region near the center.

I have fixed the sim to give a proper abort message (see attachment). The issue is that the spectrograph wave range goes just outside the primary SED range, where the primary is defined in kcor file. Another subtle issue is that the spectrograph wave range is internally extended (based on wave resolution) in order to properly account for wave-smearing near the edges. In your sim job, it adds one more wave bin, which brings the range just outside the 12600 A range of the primary SED. The simple fix is to trim the spectrograph wave range by few tens of A, and remake the kcor-input file.

this was a really evil bug. There is a check on whether SNHOST_SB__FLUXCAL exists that determines if it goes into the output tables. However, I had mistakenly made the check assuming mag (SBFLUX < 99 ==> exists) instead of FLUXCAL. In rare cases, the first event has a really bright SB where all bands have SB_FLUXCAL > 99, so the code incorrectly sets the EXIST flag to false and excludes HOST_SB from output table. If all ROOT tables but one have SB_FLUXCAL columns, the merge process fails.

It's fixed.

REDSHIFT_CMB is now computed from REDSHIFT_HELIO ... for TEXT format ... to allow quickly made data files from surveys.

body:
This is not an urgent issue things work fine as is, but sims are slower than they need to be right now:

SNANA calls `genmag_PySEDMODEL` to get the rest frame SED. This function loops through the rest frame phases and calls the python code, which returns the flux at all wavelengths at that phase. `genmag_PySEDMODEL` returns the mag and magerr lists for all phases. 

This all happens for a single filter, but then SNANA moves onto the next filter and goes through the exact same process again. The python file returns the exact same flux vs. wavelength array at all the same phases, and the only thing that changes is the integration for the new filter. If we could shift things around so the python file gets called just once per phase instead of NFILTERS time per phase, the sims would be much faster. All that needs to happen is to break this function into two, have SNANA call a new `genflux_PySEDMODEL` once to get the flux at all wavelengths at each necessary phase, then loop through filters and integrate this SED at each phase to get the correct magnitudes.

comments.body: two flags are already passed to genmag_PySEDMODEL: NEWEVENT and filter index ... so it's up to the python module to optimize itself for speed. Reducing the number of python calls would require returning multiple SEDs per call ... not clear if there's a benefit for such a refactor.

@benjaminrose I've "solved" this in BYOSED by checking to see if I've already returned the phase being requested. If yes, I know it's just another filter at the same phase and return the same flux saved in a dictionary with phases as keys and flux arrays as values. This saves the time needed to create the flux array each time if you've already done it once. Optional for you, just could speed up the sim somewhat.

@RickKessler, I don’t understand the use of a filter index inside the BOYSED framework. These are always full SEDs and have no knowlage of filters. The python code can be optimized, as described by @jpierel14, but I don’t undersand what in SNANA requires the per filter call to a full size SED. 

That being said, I totally understand if this is only a someday/maybe task that never becomes worth the optertunity cost it would take to impliment it.

snana.exe <myInput> OPT_SETPKMJD=16   TEXTFILE_PREFIX=out1

Getting a wacky error for one of my FITOPTS (not all just one...)

Reproduce here
```
cd $SNANA_DEBUG/djbrout/muerrsq
./RUNTEST
```


error below

```

   `|```````|`    
   <| o\ /o |>    
    | ' ; ' |     
    |  ___  |     ABORT program on Fatal Error. 
    | |' '| |     
    | `---' |     
    \_______/    
 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by fcn_muerrsq
   non-positive muerrsq = -2.997921e-03
   for SN = 2009D  alpha=0.180274  beta=3.100000
```

comments.body:
Fixed subtle numerical artifact in function merge_duplicate(). Nominal merged COV for duplicates is given by
    COV_merge = [ sum 1/cov_orig ]^-1 
which is inspired by the weighted average formula:  1/sigma^2 = sum[1/sigma_i^2]. For 2009D above, the COV(x1,c) element has opposite sign for the two duplicates, and the resulting sum is very close to zero, but slightly negative. This leads to a large negative COV_merge(x1,c) element, causing MUERRSQ < 0. The fix/hack is that whenever an off-diagonal element has a sign flip among the duplicates, COV_merge is the average, not the inverse-square sum above. Note that this artifact may have been present in previous analyses, but a large positive covariance could have been easily missed.

body: Current spectrograph feature in sim does not allow extrapolating TEXPOSE beyond the defined range in the spectrograph table. The result is that the sim often generates SNR values based on the min or max TEXPOSE, which can severely under-/over-estimate the desired SNR. To allow extrapolation, add a SPECTORGRAPH_MSKOPT bit to extrapolate TEXPOSE assuming SNR ~ sqrt(TEXPOSE) dependence. With this feature, a single TEXPOSE value is sufficient in the spectrograph table.

Hi Rick, 
I'm running SALT2mu.exe with alternative columns for gamma instead of HOST_LOGMASS. As such, I have instigated a MUOPT with the following entry: 
`MUOPT:  opt_biascor=2   varname_gamma='LOCAL_UR'`
replacing "HOST_LOGMASS" with "LOCAL_UR". This syntax works successfully and SALT2mu runs to conclusion. 

However, to test the sensitive of my results, I also want to cut on this variable. To do this, I had planned on using the CUTWIN function concurrently with varname_gamma. However, this doesn't seem to work; e.g.: 
`MUOPT:  opt_biascor=2   varname_gamma='LOCAL_UR'   CUTWIN LOCAL_UR 0.90 777`

results in a ABORT, stating that 'LOCAL_UR' is an invalid CUTWIN variable. This is a little weird, as, it seems that the log for the to query above lists LOCAL_UR as a viable CUTWIN variable in the LOG. 

Any thoughts on how to proceed? In short, I'd like to use the `varname_gamma` method to replace HOST_LOGMASS and then cut on it in a similar fashion to `CUTWIN HOST_LOGMASS 10 13`. 

As tests, I've tried replacing `CUTWIN LOCAL_UR` with `CUTWIN LOG_HOSTMASS` in my proposed MUOPT, but this leads to an abort. I have also tried using logmass_min/logmass_max keywords, but these cut the BIASCOR and as my parameter is not defined there this fails too. 

An example can be found: `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/DES/USERS/smithmat/SNANA_Data/DES3YR/SALT2/DES_v8/DES_only/SALT2mu_SALT2fits_local/SALT2mu_DESonly_localenv.input` 

In short - how can I cut in SALT2mu on a parameter input through the `varname_gamma` method?

Best wishes,

Mat

comments.body:
Problem is that it fails on the sim because LOCAL_UR does not exist for the sim. However, looks like this issue was solved back in October 2018. Can request DATAONLY cut with
CUTWIN(DATAONLY) LOCAL_UR 0.90 777

comments.body: ok, I think I see the problem. SALT2mu auto-detects 6D or 7D by the presence of SIM_gammaDM bins and by input nbin_logmass. But for 5D biasCor, you have the nominal SIM_gammaDM-vs-logMass from regular gamma definition. The continuous distribution (see attached) results in more than 2 SIM_gammaDM bins, so it aborts. The quick solution is to generate the biasCor sample without the gamma effects; i.e., turn off the 4 bit in HOSTLIB_MSKOPT. However, I need to think of a convenient way to force 5D even if it detects SIM_gammaDM bins.
Fixed code to ignore gammaDM dimension if more than 5 gammaDM values are found; this allows doing a 5D bias Correction with above gamma-vs-logMass profile. Update pushed to Midway.
